**Goal:** Adopt into Nessy Desktop everything upstream craft-agents-oss shipped through **v0.15.1**, with our specifics. In order:
- **security first:** the five permission defects of the v0.13.4..v0.14.0 reading (UB1.2–UB1.6), and four CRITICAL defects the v0.14.0..v0.15.1 reading found in code 1.42.0 ships (UB1.12–UB1.15: project memory rewritten from a stale copy, a cross-workspace token from the refresh single flight, `depends_on` steps started without their input, a typed credential submitted by Cancel);
- **v0.13.5–v0.14.0 as drafted on 2026-10-02:** about forty decision-free fixes, the decision layer ("System One") with upstream's five provider presets (owner answer 2026-10-02), the parity items, the carried 1.42.0 rows;
- **v0.14.1:** the decision-layer improvements (relevance filter for large results, `_intent` on source calls, per-feature usage notes, cold-start deadlines, one set of checks per message) and the sidebar truncation fix;
- **v0.15.0:** "A new look" (the redesign) and settings on a single column — both **1:1 with our specifics** (owner 2026-10-14), Claude Sonnet/Haiku 5.5, SDK 0.3.296 and Pi 1.1.0 (when the Artifactory mirror serves them), background tasks you can follow and stop, Run in background, new-chat suggestions, clean and editable labels, Pi isolation, and the fixes;
- **v0.15.1:** MCP prompts (as host session tools on all three runtimes) and resource templates, append-only project memory, Stop ends only the reply, the browser set (hidden-window input, current screenshots, fewer false security checks, quieter output, passwords out of transcripts, one sign-in popup), one sign-in for parallel sessions, guides read with `cat`, reliable task generation and step completion, attachment size checks, API keys sent as entered.

**Our specifics (standing owner rule 2026-10-14, «мы все приложение стримимся максимально близко держать к апстриму но со своей спецификой»):** three runtimes (Pi, Claude Agent SDK, Codex app-server) where upstream has two; tuned for Claude, Codex and Qwen/Nessy; the Nestor gateway (Nessy) cards, the dp login card, the BYO `claude-runtime` and codex cards, Codex/Claude runtime settings; our composer BEHAVIOUR (Codex-desktop parity: queue, 4-state submit, context meter, effort pill, capability-driven slots) under upstream's LOOK; our transcript features (verbosity modes, MessageDisplay text, orchestration progress, published-artifact chip, remember-key permission card, runtime-switch markers); en + ru only; the T-Bank network posture.

Everything ships AVAILABLE: nothing is gated (owner 2026-09-23, inherited). The decision layer's `enabled: false` default is upstream's user setting, not a gate (spec §3.4).

**Architecture:**
- The host owns every permission decision: the remember key, the allowlist inspectors, the domain grant and the source-activation pipeline are shared host functions read by Pi and Claude. Codex receives the durable rules through its execpolicy projection (F1.1057) and keeps its native `acceptForSession` and `is_known_safe_command`, each a stated residue.
- The decision layer is host-only (`packages/shared/src/decisions/`, `packages/server-core/src/decisions/`). The runtimes never see the client. Every caller falls back to today's behaviour on off, null, slow or failing. A decision never grants authority.
- New model-callable capabilities with no native counterpart on some runtime are HOST session tools on all three runtimes (AGENTS.md native-first step 2): `project_memory_append` (UB1.12), `source_list_prompts`/`source_get_prompt` (UB7.11), `decide` (UB6.11).
- The redesign is a renderer/`packages/ui` port: tokens and primitives first (Phase 13), then surfaces (Phase 14) and settings (Phase 15). Capability variance stays DATA (tool projection, `runtime-switch-costs.ts`, `ComposerCapabilities`), never renderer branches on `providerType`.

**Tech Stack:** Bun 1.3.14, TypeScript, Electron ^39 + React renderer (jotai), Tailwind v4 tokens, zod, i18n JSON (en, ru), vitepress docs-site, CDP harness in `scripts/cdp/`.

## Plan extension rule (owner 2026-10-14) — read before any row

Owner, verbatim: «можешь добавить инструкцию для агента чтоб если что он дополнил план, все равно потом тебе проверять реализацию полностью» ("you may add an instruction for the agent so that it extends the plan if needed; you will verify the implementation in full afterwards anyway").

1. **The executing agent MAY and SHOULD add rows** when a premise read, a deep-read row (UB13.1, UB14.1, UB14.42, the re-target pass UB1.18) or the implementation itself finds work this plan lacks: an upstream v0.13.5..v0.15.1 change with no row, a hunk a row's Files list misses, a Nessy specific a Keep list misses, a dependency the Needs line misses, or a defect.
2. **How:** insert the row in the OWNING phase, numbered after that phase's last id, in sorted position (never reuse or renumber an id: 1.42.0 docs cite UB ids). Give it this plan's row shape (Upstream, Files, Method and Keep for a redesign row, Tests with one positive and one negative, Runtimes, Size ≤ L, Done means) and a `**Born:**` line: date, what was found, evidence (upstream `v0.15.1:<path>` plus our `path:line`, or a measurement). Add its tracker row, then run `python3 scripts/sort-plan-tracker.py <this plan>` and `--check`.
3. **Never delete a row and never narrow one silently.** A row that turns out unnecessary closes ➖ with the reason in its note (`dropped (<reason>)`, `not taken (<measurement>)`, `result of <row or UA12.n>`). A narrower or wider scope is an amendment bullet `**Amended <date> (<why>):**` appended to the body; the original text stays.
4. **Every addition and every deviation from upstream v0.15.1** (a hunk not taken, a behaviour kept as ours, a key renamed, an upstream test not copied, a Nessy specific re-applied) gets one line in `## Extensions log`: date, row, kind (ADDED / AMENDED / DEVIATION / CLOSED), what, evidence.
5. CRITICAL findings (security, data loss, a regression this plan introduced, a red final gate, wrong user-facing behaviour) are still born and run at once (AGENTS.md). A non-critical upstream item found missing is born ⬜ in its phase (this plan's scope IS the whole upstream delta, so it is not "deferred"); a finding that is not an upstream item goes to Phase 12, born DEFERRED unless CRITICAL.
6. **The controller (Claude) verifies the whole implementation afterwards against upstream v0.15.1** (UB11.8 plus a hands-on review of every phase). Completeness beats speed: a silently skipped item costs more than an added row.

## Global Constraints

- **Git:**
  - Commit only with `git commit -F <msgfile> -- <pathspec>`, following the new-file recipe in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-07-wave-9-brief.md`.
  - Never `-m` with backticks, `--amend`, `stash`, or a bare `git add` followed by a commit. Never `checkout --`, `restore` or `reset` another lane's file.
  - Subject: `<type>(<scope>): UBx.y — <sentence>`. No `Co-Authored-By`.
  - No MR, tag, push or publish during autonomous execution.
  - One commit per row, with the recorded i18n exception: a row that introduces i18n readers lands TWO commits, keys first and reader second, its commit cell listing both shas joined by ` + `.
- **Zones:** read them from `git status` at dispatch. 0.6 lists serialised files: one row at a time across lanes.
- **Verification budget** (AGENTS.md Implementation-First):
  - In the loop: `bun scripts/bun-test-lock.ts run --label <lane> -- bun test ./<path>` with `./` on every path; **read the FILE COUNT**; the affected-package typecheck; `git diff --check`. Never pipe a gate or wrap it in `timeout`; long gates detached.
  - **Risk triggers** that expand the set once on the final diff of the row's phase: auth and permissions (Phase 1, UB7.6), shared wire/schema (UB6.1, UB6.3, UB3.4), dependency locks (Phase 8). Each such phase ends with `typecheck:all` and `lint` detached plus every UB test file of the phase, file by file.
  - Whole-repo gates run again only in UB11.7.
- **i18n:** keys in `en.json` and `ru.json` only, flat, sorted, written as characters. A row adds exactly the keys its reader uses, keys first, reader second. No locale-only rows. Upstream's de/es/hu/ja/pl/zh-Hans hunks are not ported (H15, D(c)). `check-i18n-coverage` (UA1.11) derives the key list from the row's files.
- **Settings keys:** exactly two rows add a StoredConfig key: `decisionLayer` (UB6.1) and `rtkExcludeCommands` (UB7.4). Each declares the key in `StoredConfigKnownFields` (`packages/shared/src/config/stored-config-load.ts`) per the DA1.72 docblock in `validators.ts`, and lands reader, envelope and guard fixture in ONE commit. A row that finds it needs another key is a new row with its reason.
- **Channels:**
  - Classify every new channel in `packages/shared/src/protocol/routing.ts` and map it in `apps/electron/src/transport/channel-map.ts`; regenerate `bun run scripts/ipc-inventory.ts` in the same row.
  - The one NEW module is `packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/decisions.ts` (UB6.3). It exports `HANDLED_CHANNELS`, and in the same commit adds rows to `rpc-handled-channels-agreement.test.ts`, `registration.test.ts` `getExpectedChannels` and `registration-profiles.test.ts`.
  - Every handler calls `assertCallerWorkspace` (UA1.9) where it reads workspace data. Provider, base URL and key changes are refused from a non-local client (SEC-8, UB6.3). No handler carries a feature gate.
- **Session tools:** the one new tool is `decide` (UB6.11). It updates, in ONE commit, the full Session-tools set of the UA plan's Global Constraints (`tool-defs.ts`, `HOST_CALLBACK_BRIDGE_ROUTES`, `host-callback-bridge-client.ts`, codex `session-callback-bridge.ts`, `harness-tool-descriptor.ts`, `packages/pi-agent-server/src/__tests__/harness-contract/fixtures/tool-surface.json`, `source-state-contract.ts`, `live-manifest-compositions.ts`, the `claude-agent.ts` `availableToolNames` comment, `runtime-switch-costs.ts`, the five pin tests, `packages/session-mcp-server/src/host-callback-bridge.test.ts`), then `cd packages/pi-agent-server && bun run check:surface`.
  - **Deviation from the inherited Session-tools rule (stated here, as that rule requires).** The UA plan's rule says no `SessionToolFilterOptions` field, no `isOfferedByHostPorts` arm and an `availabilityCondition` that never names a feature or switch condition. Under OQ-43.5 (a) `decide` is the exception, through the mechanism our tree already uses for host-bound capabilities (`reviewDiffPort`, `worktreePort`, `notificationPort`, `hostWebSearch` in `tool-defs.ts` `SessionToolFilterOptions`):
    - one new field `SessionToolFilterOptions.decidePort`, set by the host only when it has bound `ctx.decide` (a decision provider is configured and its settings resolve), and one `isOfferedByHostPorts` arm for `decide`;
    - `availabilityCondition` wording, modelled on the existing `reviewDiffPort` row: "requires SessionToolFilterOptions.decidePort (the host has bound ctx.decide: a decision provider is configured); externalStandaloneOnly excludes it as host-callback dependent unless the bridge carries HOST_CALLBACK_BRIDGE_ROUTES.decide";
    - why this is a capability condition, not a gate: it names whether the thing the tool calls EXISTS (a configured provider), exactly as `reviewDiffPort` names whether the host bound a reviewer. No env, build or managed switch can hide it; the user's own Settings choice is the only input, and a Settings diagnostic says why the tool is absent (spec §3.4);
    - pins: `tool-defs-filtering.test.ts` (offered with the port, absent without it), the five pin tests' counts with and without the port, and `external-standalone.test.ts` for the codex bridge arm.
- **Copying:**
  - Rebrand `Craft`→`Nessy`, `@craft-agent`→`@nessy-agent`, `CRAFT_`→`NESSY_`, `~/.craft-agent`→`CONFIG_DIR`/`NESSY_CONFIG_DIR`, `craft-*` localStorage→`nessy-*`; drop `X-Title: Craft Agents`. "Jev", "Laya" and "TypeSafe" are the provider's names and stay where a shipped string names them.
  - Copied files record `v0.14.0:<path>` (or `v0.13.6:`/`v0.13.5:`) in their header. Adapted prompt and policy text records its source and licence (Apache-2.0; LICENSE and NOTICE kept).
  - Shipped docs are REWRITTEN in our words, land with their code, and describe what OUR code does (spec §3.1; the loop-guard bullet is the measured counter-example).
- **The manifest is authoritative for file→row.** Re-derive a row's Files list from it before dispatch.
- **Network posture (T-Bank, spec §3.5):** model traffic goes through the Nestor gateway (`Nestor-Token` only on the verified URL) or the user's own BYO connection. No row adds a third-party service that receives session content without an owner decision (OQ-43.2, OQ-43.9, OQ-43.10). A loopback service the user runs is not egress. An installer command or an external docs link shown in the UI is posture too (OQ-43.8, OQ-43.2b), and so is where a package or model weights are fetched from (OQ-43.2b).
- **Three runtimes:** every row carries a `Runtimes:` line naming its reach on Pi, Claude (Agent SDK) and Codex (app-server), or a stated residue, in that native-first order (spec §3.3). A host-only or renderer-only row writes "runtime-neutral" and says why. A codex claim from a docs page alone is a hypothesis; the source or the binary outranks it.
- **Native-first:** every BUILD row (one that adds code rather than copying a fix into code that already exists) carries a `Native-first:` line naming what it found when it asked whether the runtime already has the capability, with the evidence read (a Claude page named in words, codex source, the Pi SDK), or the searched-and-absent null.
- **Measure rows:** every `[measure]` row names its instrument, a control that can fail on the same instrument (AGENTS.md: every absence claim needs a positive control), and its result file. Its Done means is "the result file records the reading, the control's reading and the decision", not "tests pass".
- **Playground:** extend canonical entries with knobs (decision card states, risk badges, the rtk dialog, workspace avatars, the permission card with and without a remember key), and sweep all states in dark theme.
- **Tests:** every invariant gets at least one positive and one negative test, named in the row (the "control"). A row with no explicit Done means is done when every named arm passes alone with the expected FILE COUNT, its affected-package typecheck is green, and every file in its re-derived Files list is committed.
- **Live cases:** sitting cases are `scripts/cdp/cases/rs-NNN.ts` with `meta.row` naming the UB row, registered in `scripts/cdp/run.ts` `SITTING`. **RS ids are allocated by the controller at dispatch** and its "case owed (UBx.y)" checklist row is written in a pin commit; `rs-109.ts` exists on 2026-10-02. Driven in each phase's packaged sitting (the `env -u` launcher, `bypassPermissions` unless the card is the subject, dark theme) and again in UB11.5. A permission-card case runs in the mode that raises the card, never bypass.
- **No real credentials.** No row reads or prints one. The decisions key and the masked-key test use fixture values only.


**Amendments to the Global Constraints (2026-10-14, the v0.15.1 widening).** Where a bullet above and one below disagree, the one below wins.
- **Upstream version:** rows port `v0.15.1:<path>`. Copied files record `v0.15.1:<path>` in their header (not `v0.14.0:`), plus the tag where the change first appeared when a row names it. Adapted prompt and policy text records its source and licence (Apache-2.0; LICENSE and NOTICE kept), as before.
- **Session tools (replaces "the one new tool is `decide`"):** this plan adds FOUR session tools: `decide` (UB6.11, offered through `decidePort` as stated above), `project_memory_append` (UB1.12), `source_list_prompts` and `source_get_prompt` (UB7.11). Each row lands the FULL Session-tools set in ONE commit (`tool-defs.ts`, `HOST_CALLBACK_BRIDGE_ROUTES`, `host-callback-bridge-client.ts`, codex `session-callback-bridge.ts`, `harness-tool-descriptor.ts`, `tool-surface.json`, `source-state-contract.ts`, `live-manifest-compositions.ts`, the `claude-agent.ts` `availableToolNames` comment, `runtime-switch-costs.ts`, the five pin tests, `host-callback-bridge.test.ts`, `SESSION_TOOL_DISPLAY_NAMES` in `packages/shared/src/utils/toolNames.ts`), then `cd packages/pi-agent-server && bun run check:surface`. Rows touching that set are serialised (0.6b). The three new tools carry NO feature condition (upstream offers them unconditionally); `project_memory_append` refuses a session with no bound project, `source_*_prompts` answer honestly when a source offers no prompts.
- **Settings keys (widens "exactly two rows"):** besides `decisionLayer` (UB6.1) and `rtkExcludeCommands` (UB7.4), a Phase 13–15 row that finds upstream v0.15.1 persists a new preference (the Motion preference, UB13.4, is the known one) declares it by the DA1.72 recipe in ONE commit and lists it in the Extensions log. Any other new key is a new row with its reason.

The Motion preference persists in the renderer theme record (localStorage `nessy-theme`, the `lib/local-storage.ts` PREFIX) and travels on the existing theme-preference broadcast with a type-only `motion?` field (R1-04, UB13.4); R2's width changes are `storage.get` fallbacks only. "Exactly two rows" (`decisionLayer`, `rtkExcludeCommands`) holds again; a row that finds otherwise is a new row with its reason.

Each classifies in `routing.ts`, maps in `channel-map.ts`, regenerates `ipc-inventory`, and is a shared-wire risk trigger.

Every new user-visible string needs BOTH keys, keys commit first, reader second; `bun run lint:i18n:parity` and `bun run lint:i18n:sorted` green on every row that touches a locale. Upstream's de/es/hu/ja/pl/zh-Hans hunks are D(c). Where upstream still ships an English literal and ours has a key, keep ours (Keep lists name them).

The row records which and why.

## Review Focus

1. **The remember key equals the click.** No key is wider than the approved argv's class; an exact-argv key persists as `Bash(<whole line>)` without ` *` and is matched exactly; Pi's PermissionRequest suggestion is built from the same key and destination equality is enforced; the curl domain grant covers single plain commands to whitelisted hosts only. Each on Pi, Claude and the codex projection.
2. **The argv inspectors.** Every refused spelling pinned (attached and clustered forms), and both arms: real reads (`sort -k`, `sed -n p`, `gh api` GET) stay read-only.
3. **Source activation re-runs the whole pipeline** (UB1.6). A default-mode `prompt` stays a card; the guardian deny-net is consulted on the re-run.
4. **The decision layer has zero authority.** Every caller returns today's behaviour on null, off, slow or failing; no state text is written to disk; no provider, base URL or key change from a remote client; no `Nestor-Token` off the verified URL; paths are under `CONFIG_DIR`.
5. **Transparency.** Every automatic action taken on a decision (a status move, a label, a skipped automation, an inferred verdict, a narrowed repair) shows its source and probability to the user.
6. **No gating.** The layer's off default is a user setting; no env, build or managed switch. Dropped features' toggles are absent, not hidden.
7. **Three runtimes.** Each row states Pi, Claude and Codex reach or a residue; codex docs-only claims are hypotheses.
8. **UB4.8 diverges from upstream on purpose.** The target (not true at HEAD: our `PendingPrompt` carries no `event`/`eventPayload`) is that `buildPendingPromptsForMatchers` always sets them. The controls go through our real paths: `PromptHandler` or the missed-run catch-up sweep (`AutomationSystem.runMissedRunSweep`) → `buildPendingPromptsForMatchers` → the `onPromptsReady` closure in `SessionManager.ts` → `executePromptAutomation`. Upstream's `runReadyPrompts` does not exist in ours.
9. **New StoredConfig keys** (`decisionLayer`, `rtkExcludeCommands`) follow the DA1.72 recipe in one commit each.
10. **The new RPC module** (`rpc/decisions.ts`): `HANDLED_CHANNELS`, the three registration tests, `ipc-inventory`, `routing.ts` classes.
11. **i18n.** About 82 `settings.ai.decisions.*` keys (minus the dropped features' rows) plus the feature keys, en+ru, each with its reader.
12. **Rebrand.** No `Craft`, `craft-agent`, `CRAFT_` or `thecraftagents` string ships (extend UA6.6's guard if needed).
13. **No posture decided quietly.** Every new endpoint preset, installer command or widening of what runs without a card cites its OQ.

14. **The four CRITICAL rows of the delta (UB1.12–UB1.15).** Two concurrent appends both survive and no prompt still says "Write/Edit MEMORY.md"; two workspaces with one slug never share a refreshed token; a `depends_on` dependent receives the upstream reply exactly once; Cancel on the credential form sends exactly one response, `cancelled: true`.
15. **The redesign is LOOK 1:1, BEHAVIOUR ours.** Every Keep item of a Phase 13–15 row is still reachable and pinned; no Craft URL, brand or global ships; `@nessy-agent/ui` barrel-free imports kept where the barrel trap applies (R6); the guardrail lint count only goes down (UB13.14).
16. **The four new session tools** land with the full Session-tools set each (Global Constraints amendments) and reach Pi, Claude and Codex (codex through the bridge).
17. **Completeness against v0.15.1.** `d15-map.py` maps 615 of 615 paths; every release-note item of 0.14.1/0.15.0/0.15.1 has a Feature-inventory line; every deviation is in the Extensions log.
18. **The `--*-rgb` sweep and the theme switch (added 2026-10-14, R1).** After UB13.3 no reader of a removed triplet remains (`var(` and quoted forms, incl. `BrowserShader`'s JS read); UB13.3 and UB13.4 ship in one release; our six presets + Paper pass AA under upstream's solver; no `craft.json` and no "Craft Agents" label ships.

**Readers of this file (once promoted):**
- `python3 scripts/sort-plan-tracker.py <this file> --check`: rows form one family, `UB<phase>.<n>`, sorted numerically.
- `--shas` (`lint:plan-shas`): commit cells hold `—` or real shas; in-cell pipes are written as "or".
- `scripts/plan-status.py` `VERDICT_SOURCE_PLANS` and `scripts/cdp/harness.test.ts` `PLANS` get this plan in UB1.1.
- `build-parity-report.py` and `regenerate-deviation-register.py` read its full text; regenerated in UB11.6.
- `check-doc-anchors.ts`: Claude pages are named in words, never by anchor.

**Deviation recorded (inherited):** the controller pins rows (glyph + sha) in `docs(plan): <lane> pinned — …` commits. Lanes do not edit this file.

**UB1.2 `[security]` `[CRITICAL]` `[pi]` `[claude]` `[codex]` The Always Allow key equals the click (M; OQ-43.3b; SEC-1) → pointer to UA12.n.**
- **Needs:** none.
- **Premise:** re-run the remember-key probe at HEAD; every "approve X → later call with NO card" pair of spec §4 SEC-1 (`git clean -n`→`git clean -fdx`, `git branch`→`git branch -D main`, `python3 script.py`→`… --delete-all`, `node -e "…"`→`node evil.js`, `npx prettier --check .`→`--write .`, …) still auto-allows.
- **Upstream:** v0.14.0 `packages/shared/src/agent/core/permission-remember.ts` `getBashRememberKey` (at most 3 leading words; interpreters and runners keyed on exact argv; no key for wrappers, `gh api`, a flag before the subcommand, or a destructive word); the grown `DANGEROUS_COMMANDS`; `PermissionRequest.tsx` hiding Always Allow when no key.
- **Native-first:** Claude's own dialog stores the whole line (the hooks page, its PermissionRequest example), so upstream now matches native. Codex keeps `acceptForSession` and `proposedExecpolicyAmendment` natively (residue, UB1.7). **Not adopted:** upstream's FILE-WRITE key, `getFileWriteRememberKey` (`write:<folder>`, one Always Allow covers every later write into that folder). Ours keys a file write per path (`pre-tool-use.ts` `fileWriteWhitelistKey`, `${toolName}:${filePath}`, D1.306) and an API call per exact method and path (D1.306); both are narrower than upstream, a deliberate reason-(b)/(c) divergence recorded in the Feature inventory (KEEP).
- **Files:** `packages/shared/src/agent/core/dangerous-commands.ts` (`bashSessionWhitelistKey`, `DANGEROUS_COMMANDS`); `core/bash-remember-scope.ts`; `SessionManager.ts` `persistBashAlwaysAllowRule` (an exact-argv key persists as `Bash(<whole line>)` with no ` *`); the durable consult in `pre-tool-use.ts` (`bashSessionGrantCoversLine`) matches an exact key exactly, never by prefix; `packages/core/src/types/message.ts` (upstream's `canRemember?: boolean` on the permission request, v0.14.0, the "no key, no Always Allow" signal; the `risks` hunk of the same file is UB6.10's); `PermissionRequest.tsx` (no key → no Always Allow; D1.262's relabel kept); the five `chat.permission*` keys only if ours lacks equivalents (keys commit first).

**UB2.2 `[claude]` Stop on Claude: no re-send, no lost text, no cross-query teardown (M; COR-2 + the v0.14.0 keep-alive Stop hunks).**
- **Upstream (v0.14.0 `claude-agent.ts`, four decision-free hunks of the `v0.13.4..v0.14.0` diff, all part of "Stop no longer re-runs your message"; `claude-keepalive-stop.test.ts`):**
  1. a Stop marks `activeTurnState.aborted`, and the persistent turn throws `AbortError` instead of reaching the empty-response recovery (the COR-2 fix proper);
  2. the `AbortError` branch calls `eventAdapter.flushPending()` first, so a finished text block that was waiting for its `message_delta` is not missing after a reload;
  3. each consumer is bound to its own query (`persistentConsumerIterator`): a message from an older query is skipped, and the consumer's `finally` tears down only the query it served, never a newer one (an aborted query's consumer may still be draining when the next turn starts);
  4. a Stop while the turn is being prepared (`AbortError` from the outer `try`, e.g. during the keep-alive thinking update) yields `complete`: an interruption, not an error.
- **Premise (read at `49f505fd5`):** (1) our post-loop recovery (`wasResuming && !receivedAssistantContent && !_isRetry`) has no `user_stop` guard (R14-11); (2) our `AbortError` branch (`claude-agent.ts` ≈L10179) has no `flushPending`: the only flush is in the no-result region (≈L10142), which a Stop never reaches; (3) ours has no `persistentIterator`/consumer: our keep-alive is `backend/claude/live-session.ts` (`ClaudeInputChannel`, the turn slot of `turn-slot.ts`), so the row READS that design for the same race (a slot of an aborted query receiving a later query's messages, or tearing a newer one down) and records the verdict; (4) read whether any `await` between Stop and the turn's first message can throw `AbortError` outside the inner `try`.
- **Measure first (on `claude-gateway`, packaged):** (a) Stop within about 1 s of sending turn 2: the message must not re-run; (b) Stop mid-answer after one finished text block, then reload the session: is that block present? Controls: a turn left to finish keeps all its blocks; a Stop on turn 1 still clears the empty session as today.
- **Files:** `claude-agent.ts` (the recovery guard: skip when the turn ended on `user_stop` or `max_budget_usd`; `flushPending` at the top of the `AbortError` branch; the outer-catch interruption arm only if (4) finds a path); `backend/claude/live-session.ts`/`turn-slot.ts` only if (3) finds the race.
- **Tests:** `claude-resume-recovery-stop.test.ts` (new; upstream `claude-keepalive-stop.test.ts` cases adapted). Positive: a resumed turn with no assistant content and no stop still recovers; a text block pending at Stop is emitted once as `text_complete`. Negative (control): `user_stop` and `max_budget_usd` do not clear the session id and do not re-send; with nothing pending the flush emits nothing; if (3) applies, a late message of an aborted query never reaches the next turn's slot.
- **Native-first:** the SDK's own `interrupt()` is what we call; the recovery and the flush are ours, nothing native replaces them.
- **Runtimes:** Claude only (the four hunks are the Claude keep-alive). Pi: Stop goes through the subprocess abort, no recovery re-send (n/a). Codex: `turn/interrupt`, native (n/a).
- **Amended 2026-10-14 (B2-12, RT):** read v0.15.1 `claude-keepalive-stop.test.ts` (+79) and `backend/types.ts` `stopTurn()` (interrupt without closing the query; leftovers dropped up to the stopped turn's `result`; a 10 s fallback hard stop). Our Claude Stop is HAVE (SDK `interrupt()`, query kept; escalation at 5 s, `INTERRUPT_DEADLINE_MS`); point (3) of this row is where the leftover-isolation reading lands. The Pi and codex arms of "Stop ends only the reply" are UB2.10.
- **Amended 2026-10-14 (RT, beyond B2-12):** the upstream set is the four v0.14.0 hunks above PLUS v0.15.1 `claude-agent.ts` `stopTurn()` (marks the turn aborted, ends the channel, `pendingSteers.pause()`, clears `toolHandoff`, then a cooperative `interrupt()`), the `stoppedTurn` consumer filter (leftovers up to the stopped turn's `result` are dropped, but background notifications among them still go through `routeBackgroundMessage`), the `STOPPED_TURN_RESULT_WAIT_MS` 10 s hard stop with teardown nulling `currentQuery`, and the four `stopTurn` cases of `claude-keepalive-stop.test.ts`. Premise (3) adds: after OUR Stop (`interruptLiveTurn`, query kept), do the stopped turn's trailing messages before its `result` reach the next turn's slot? Keep `INTERRUPT_DEADLINE_MS` 5 s (logged DEVIATION, UB2.10). Added negative test: a stopped turn's leftover text never reaches turn N+1, and a `task_notification` among the leftovers reaches the background sink.

- **Upstream:** v0.13.6 #1058/#1060, decision-free, on BOTH Pi and Claude: `AgentBackend.isCompactionInFlight?()` (`backend/types.ts`, `base-agent.ts`), read by `SessionManager` (v0.14.0 L1210 `shouldAttemptMidStreamSteer`, L6442) so a mid-stream message is QUEUED for replay during a manual compaction; `PiAgent.isCompactionInFlight` (a pending compact RPC) plus `redirect()` refusing in that state; `ClaudeAgent.isCompactionInFlight()` = `isProcessing() && eventAdapter.isManualCompactionRequested()` (Claude steers are delivered at the next tool call, which a compaction turn never makes); the compact timeout bumps the epoch and aborts; `packages/pi-agent-server/src/compaction-wait.ts` bounds the wait (name collides with our renderer `input/compaction-wait.ts`: the new file keeps upstream's path, which is a different package).

**UB2.8 `[tasks]` `[host]` TaskRunner v0.15.1 completion arms: a stopped step waits, a stopped verify turn is not the verdict, an empty reply fails (M; B4-15, B4-17, B4-19; OQ-B4-3 (a)).**

What remains: (a) the user's continuing turn is then ignored (`st.state !== 'running'`) and Resume re-dispatches the node in a NEW child, losing the steer; a `timeout` from a Stop FAILS or retries the node (inconsistent with item 9); our completion event has no `fromUser`; (b) `attachVerdictListener` takes the next completion whatever its reason, so a Stop during verify triggers `reAskVerdict` and overrides the user's Stop; (c) `completeNode` fails an empty reply only when `outputs` are declared.
- **Upstream:** v0.15.1 `server-core/src/tasks/TaskRunner.ts` (`waitingForUser`, `node-waiting` log, `fromUser`; verdict listener skips `interrupted`/`timeout`; `'finished without a reply'`), `tasks/storage.ts` (`node-waiting` entry), `SessionManager` (`stopEpoch` → `interrupted`, `fromUser` on the completion event), `session-completion.test.ts`, `TaskRunner.test.ts`.

(b) the verdict listener ignores `interrupted`/`timeout`; an unparsed verdict at an UNSETTLED door (`host.isSessionSettled`, ours, not upstream's count) waits for the next door. (c) an accepted completion with empty text fails the node (retry policy applies).

Negative (control): an `error` still fails at once; a settled unparsed reply still re-asks (bounded 2); a deferred door's non-empty text (UA12.100) still completes.

The HOST half (pi-agent.ts: on this message move the entry out of the Stop sweep into the background set, `stop_background_task` still stopping it) waits on the UB7.4 lane's hold of pi-agent.ts; the packaged Pi drive stays the sitting ASK.

The CODE is complete; what remains of the row is exactly its [measure] arm — the packaged Pi drive (Stop with a detached MCP call running: `mcp-background-task-stopped` vs a result) — the sitting ASK. **UB2.15 `[pi]` Port upstream's provider-level retry block (`retry.provider`) onto our Pi retry profiles (S; born 2026-10-15 from UB5.3's measurement).**
- **Born:** 2026-10-15, from UB5.3's measurement (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-15-ub5-3-provider-retry-after.md`): pi-ai `0.87.1` honours `retry-after` at the provider level under `{maxRetries: 2, maxRetryDelayMs: 60_000}` (measured gaps [7003, 7006] ms, one agent attempt, the stacked ladder untouched) and shows its own ≤8 s backoff without the header ([474, 888] ms); with the block ABSENT — our shipped wiring, `git grep maxRetryDelayMs` = 0 hits — the 429 reaches the agent ladder ([2025, 4009] ms on the 3 × 2 s off-gateway profile) and the header is discarded. Upstream v0.15.1 ships the block as its default (`v0.15.1:packages/pi-agent-server/src/session-settings.ts`, `CRAFT_PI_RETRY_SETTINGS.provider`), measured better for gateway and BYO alike: a limiter 429 costs two header-directed sleeps instead of re-rolling whole assistant turns on the 15 s × 5 ladder.
- **Upstream:** v0.15.1 `packages/pi-agent-server/src/session-settings.ts` (the `provider` blocks: main `{maxRetries: 2, maxRetryDelayMs: 60_000}`, ephemeral `{2, 10_000}`), consumed by pi-ai's `retryProviderRequest` (vendored `utils/provider-retry.js`).
- **Files:** `packages/pi-agent-server/src/gateway-retry-settings.ts` (add `provider` to the four frozen profiles and to `resolveRetrySettings`' returns — agent numbers untouched); the applyOverrides shape carries it (`applyRetryPolicy` needs no signature change).
- **Method:** stack, don't replace: the measured agent ladders (P6.273: gateway 5 × 15 s, off-gateway 3 × 2 s, utility 2 × 15 s / 2 × 2 s) stay; each profile gains `provider` (main 2/60 s, utility 2/10 s — upstream's numbers; `NESSY_MAX_API_RETRIES` keeps moving only `maxRetries`). The 60 s cap also bounds a hostile header: a longer server delay fails the request at once (`provider-retry.js:22-28`) into the agent ladder.
- **Tests:** positive: `resolveRetrySettings(true)` returns `{maxRetries: 5, baseDelayMs: 15_000, provider: {maxRetries: 2, maxRetryDelayMs: 60_000}}` (and the utility profile the 10 s cap) — extend `gateway-retry-settings.test.ts`; negative (control): `NESSY_MAX_API_RETRIES` still overrides only `maxRetries` and never `provider`, and an unset-env return stays reference-equal to the frozen profiles where it was before.
- **Runtimes:** Pi only (the provider block is pi-ai's; Claude and codex have their own retry stacks).
- **Size:** S. **Done means:** both profiles carry the block, both test arms green, `check:surface` unaffected (settings-only). Residue carried from UB5.3: the subprocess anomaly (a turn ending after one 429 with `willRetry: true` and no continuation under the reduced harness) — one packaged-sitting drive confirms the live ladder before or with this row.

**UB3.3 `[auth]` `[security]` RFC 8707 resource from RFC 9728 metadata (M; R14-18).**
- **Why `[security]` and why not CRITICAL:** the `resource` parameter binds an OAuth token to its intended audience, a token-replay control the MCP authorization spec requires; without it a token minted for one server is not audience-bound. It is not CRITICAL because no misuse is measured: today's observable effect is functional (resource-bound MCP servers reject our tokens), and no token of ours was shown accepted by a server it was not minted for. It stays in Phase 3, ordered first among the Phase 3 lanes.

- **Runtimes:** host OAuth, runtime-neutral (all three read the same stored token).

**UB4.17 `[electron]` `[pi]` `[claude]` Fewer false security checks: a classifier confirmed on a second look (M; B5-03).**
- **Premise:** BPM (≈L1831) pushes `ax:near-empty(…)` as a signal and `detected = signals.length > 0`, so any sparse a11y tree (an open Radix menu, a consent page, an error card) is a "challenge"; the bare `/Verify you are human/` matches embedded widgets; the runtime then `releaseControl()`s and prints "Browser shown" without showing it, after EVERY click.
- **Upstream:** v0.15.1 NEW `apps/electron/src/main/security-challenge.ts` (+ test), BPM `checkSecurityChallenge` + `classifySecurityChallenge`, re-check after 750 ms, no verdict while loading or when the URL changed; runtime `handChallengeToUser` (`releaseControl` + `focusWindow`, honest text when the window cannot be shown), `suspectedChallengeNote`; `BrowserSecurityChallenge` DTO with `suspected` (`protocol/dto.ts`).
- **Method:** take (CV). Pins to re-read: `browser-tools.test.ts` ≈L140, ≈L345–359.
- **Tests:** positive: a Cloudflare interstitial is detected after the re-check. Negative (control): an open Radix menu with 2 actionable nodes is not detected and control is kept.
- **Runtimes:** Pi and Claude; Codex n/a.

**UB4.18 `[shared]` `[pi]` `[claude]` Screenshot metadata as compact lines (S; B5-04).**
- **Premise:** `browser-tool-runtime.ts` (≈L1097, ≈L1179) appends `'Metadata:', JSON.stringify(result.metadata, null, 2)` (≈15k tokens); BPM caps at the first 100 refs in document order, off-screen ones included.
- **Upstream:** v0.15.1 `formatScreenshotMetadata`/`formatScreenshotTarget` (≤ 50 targets, "at (x,y) WxH", warnings, last action, region); BPM annotates ON-SCREEN elements only.
- **Tests:** positive: 100 targets → 50 lines + "…50 more". Negative (control): no `Metadata:` JSON block in any screenshot output.
- **Runtimes:** Pi and Claude; Codex n/a.

**UB4.19 `[electron]` `[pi]` `[claude]` Console and network logs scoped to the committed site (M; B5-05).**
- **Needs:** UB4.6.
- **Premise:** BPM `pushNetworkLog(instance, entry)` (≈L3310) has no scoping; console push (≈L3778) has no internal-page filter; no `did-start-navigation` handler.
- **Upstream:** v0.15.1 BPM `onInternalPage`, `internalRequestIds`, `requestStartedAt`/`networkEntryStartedAt`, `pendingNavigation`, `scopeLogsToCommittedPage` on `did-navigate`, `pushNetworkLog(instance, requestId, entry)`.
- **Method:** merge around OUR P6.360 download-policy hunks (≈L3324–3387, ≈L3477–3523); use the lookup UB4.6 leaves.
- **Tests:** positive: navigating A→B drops A's entries and A's late finishers. Negative (control): a same-site navigation keeps them; the empty-state page's requests are never logged.
- **Runtimes:** Pi and Claude; Codex n/a.

**UB4.20 `[shared]` `[security]` `[pi]` `[claude]` `browser_tool` quote rule in the SHARED parser (S; B5-06, B5-10 quoting).**
- **Premise:** our parser lives in `browser-tool-command-parse.ts` (toggle-quote rule; `throw 'unclosed quote'`), so `fill @e5 Don't do this` fails; `browser-tools.md` (≈L105) promises `\;` for a literal semicolon, but `decodeEscapes` keeps the backslash; the runtime runs the RAW single command while the classifier classifies the split one.
- **Upstream:** v0.15.1 `browser-tool-runtime.ts` `findClosingQuote` (a quote opens only at token start and closes at the same quote followed by whitespace, `;` or end; mid-token pairs still protect `;`), `decodeEscapes` gains `\;`, empty split → "Missing command", a single command runs `commands[0]`; docs quoting section.
- **ADAPT (security-relevant placement):** the rule lands in `browser-tool-command-parse.ts`, NOT in the runtime: that module is shared by the plan-mode classifier (`isReadOnlyBrowserToolInput`, `browser-tool-names.ts` ≈L174–209) and the executor, and a parser change in one place only is the gate/executor desync bypass its header warns about. Update the classifier's docblock. Docs rewritten in our wording.
- **Tests:** positive: `fill @e5 Don't do this` fills "Don't do this"; `\;` decodes. Negative (control): `isReadOnlyBrowserToolInput('snapshot; click @e1')` stays false, and an unclosed token-start quote still throws in BOTH the classifier and the executor.
- **Runtimes:** Pi and Claude; Codex n/a.

**UB4.21 `[electron]` `[pi]` `[claude]` One sign-in popup per origin across browser windows of one workspace (S; B5-08, B5-14).**
- **Needs:** UB4.6.
- **Premise:** `setWindowOpenHandler` (BPM ≈L3806) has no cross-window sign-in check; one cookie partition `persist:browser-pane` for all panes.
- **Upstream:** v0.15.1 BPM `isSignInPopupUrl`, `findOpenSignInPopup` (deny + `moveTop()` the open one), `recordPopupEvent`/`describePopupEvents` reported through `clickElement`'s `popup`, `popupOpenedOriginByWebContentsId`.

Restrict the search to the SAME workspace; name the choice in a comment and the Extensions log.

## Phase 5: Measurements (`UB5.1`–`UB5.6`)

Each row closes as a recorded result, or spawns a take row in the right phase. Every row names an instrument, a control that can fail on the same instrument, and a result file `docs/superpowers/specs/<date>-ub5-<n>-<slug>.md` (Global Constraints, "Measure rows").

**UB5.1 `[claude]` `[measure]` Recorded system prompt carries nothing per-turn (XS; R14-32).** SDK 0.3.274 records the system prompt by default; read our append and confirm it carries no per-turn or per-mode value (a recorded prompt freezes it until compaction). Instrument: the SDK transcript of a two-turn session with a mode switch between turns. Control: a deliberately per-turn line planted in a scratch build is visible frozen. Result file as above. Runtimes: Claude only (Pi and codex rebuild per turn; n/a).
- **Amended 2026-10-14 (RT):** HEAD's SDK is 0.3.280 (UA12.211); measure there and re-read on 0.3.296 with UB8.1.

**UB5.2 `[claude]` `[measure]` `/compact` success with no boundary (S; H5).** On 2.1.274, `/compact` on a too-small conversation: does it answer `result(success)` with no manual boundary, leaving an Accept & Compact plan pending? Instrument: the SDK message stream of the turn (our event-adapter debug log) on `claude-gateway`, both self-reports recorded. Control (can fail): the same `/compact` on a conversation long enough to compact must show the boundary, else the instrument misses boundaries. Decision rule: success with no boundary → port upstream's correlation (v0.13.4 `claude-compaction-events.test.ts`); a boundary or an error → treat it like F1.856 (nothing to compact) and record. Result file as above. Runtimes: Claude only.

**UB5.3 `[pi]` `[measure]` Provider pre-stream retries against the gateway limiter (S; H7).** Does pi-ai honour the gateway's `retry-after` under `{maxRetries:2, maxRetryDelayMs:60000}` stacked under our 15 s × 5 ladder? Instrument: a loopback stub that answers 429 with `retry-after: 7` twice, then 200, driven through the Pi subprocess with the settings block, timestamps of each request recorded. Control (can fail): the same stub without `retry-after` must show pi-ai's own backoff, and with the block absent the first 429 must reach our ladder. Decide for BYO and gateway separately; the gateway default stays as is unless measured better. Result file as above. Runtimes: Pi only.

**UB5.4 `[renderer]` `[measure]` Composer at 150–200 % zoom in a short window (S; H12).** Electron only (webui dormant, D(c)). Instrument: the CDP harness at 150 % and 200 % zoom, window 900×600, a 20-line draft in the composer; read the composer's `getBoundingClientRect()` against the viewport. Control (can fail): the same reading at 100 % in a 1400×900 window must show the composer inside the viewport; a deliberately oversized `inputMaxHeight` in a scratch build must read outside. Take upstream's `input-viewport`/`composer-height` only if the composer leaves the visible area. Result file as above. Runtimes: renderer-only, runtime-neutral.

**UB5.5 `[electron]` `[measure]` Update handoff rehearsal (M; H28, OQ-43.11).** `scripts/verify-update-feed.mjs` plus a packaged install over a running app: is the update installed, or does `quit-finalizer.ts`'s `preventDefault`-then-re-quit leave it downloaded-but-not-installed? Instrument: the installed app's version from both the bundle's `Info.plist` and the app's own About/version report after relaunch, plus `<config dir>/logs/boot.log`. Control (can fail): a rehearsal with the update feed pointing at the SAME version must report "no update", else the feed reading is wrong. Adopt upstream's `performQuitCleanup` before `quitAndInstall` only on the second outcome. Signed confirmation stays the reviewer's. Result file as above. Runtimes: Electron main, runtime-neutral.

**UB5.6 `[pi]` `[claude]` `[measure]` How often and how slowly `guardLargeResult` summarises (S; DEC-12).** On the `fast` alias over a representative sitting: count and latency of `guardLargeResult` summaries (`packages/shared/src/utils/large-response.ts`). Instrument: a debug counter and timer around the summary call (scratch build), the sitting's case list named. Control (can fail): one planted oversized tool result must be counted once with a latency > 0, else the counter is not wired. Decision rule written before the reading: UB6.16 is taken only if summaries exceed a stated share of tool calls AND a stated median latency. The result decides UB6.16 only. Result file as above. Runtimes: Pi and Claude (host guard); codex truncates natively (n/a).
- **Amended 2026-10-14 (B1-01):** also record the share of summarised results that carry an `_intent`, per runtime (0 for MCP sources until UB3.9). UB6.16 now ports the v0.15.1 relevance filter; this measurement still decides whether it is taken.

> **Amended 2026-10-14:** the owner answered OQ-43.2 and OQ-43.2b on 2026-10-02 (upstream parity: TypeSafe, OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway, Laya, Custom; the master switch off by default; upstream's gate order). The ⏸ sentence below is superseded: Phase 6 rows read ⬜ and are dispatched after Phases 2–5 (core unit first); UB6.18 stays ⛔. The decision layer changed again in v0.14.1 (large-result relevance filter, usage notes, cold deadlines, one set of checks per message) and v0.15.0 (semantic labels by meaning, decision tone): rows port v0.15.1 and carry the B1 amendments below. Where a feature's live case may get a provider from is OQ-43.13.

**Every row here reads ⏸ until the OWNER answers OQ-43.2 and OQ-43.2b; the controller does not take their defaults** (Sequencing). Under (e) every row closes `dropped (OQ-43.2 (e))`. The core unit is UB6.1–UB6.5; feature rows follow OQ-43.6b's order and ship only with a PASSED case (Sequencing, "One rule for Phase 6 feature rows"). Native-first for the whole phase: no runtime has a typed probability classifier; the layer is built once in the host and never seen by a runtime (spec §6.A). **Runtimes for every Phase 6 row unless the row says otherwise:** host-only, runtime-neutral: the client, the decision point and every feature read host state (session text, task output, permission requests), so Pi, Claude and codex sessions get the same behaviour; a row that touches a runtime surface (UB6.10 codex, UB6.11, UB6.13, UB6.16) states it.

**UB6.18 `[gateway]` A "Nessy Gateway" decision provider (S; OQ-43.2 (b)) — ⛔ until the gateway team publishes a decision route.**
- **Opens only when** the Nestor gateway team publishes a Jev-compatible route (`…/v1/systemone` or another), with its wire, alias and response shape documented. Until then nothing is built: no preset, no probe, no request from any client.

- **Runtimes:** host-only, runtime-neutral.

## Port manifest

**How to read it.**
- **Tags:** `.5` = v0.13.5, `.6` = v0.13.6, `.14` = v0.14.0: the tags in which the path changed after v0.13.4 (`git diff --name-only` per tag pair). Read the path at the LAST tag named.
- **Lines:** `+added/−removed` from `git diff --numstat v0.13.4 v0.14.0` ("hunk" = feature hunks only).
- **Disposition codes:** CV copy-verbatim · CA copy+adapt · RW rewrite · D(a)/D(b)/D(c) drop with reason · KEEP already ours · MEAS measure, then decide · OQ owner question · PTR carried by pointer to a 1.42.0 row · N/A packaging or version churn with no behaviour for us.
- **Added 2026-10-14:** tag codes `.14.1` = v0.14.1, `.15.0` = v0.15.0, `.15.1` = v0.15.1. Sections K–N cover `git diff v0.14.0 v0.15.1` by path group (`d15-map.py`, UB1.17, gives the per-path map). A path of A–J that changed again after v0.14.0 is ported at v0.15.1; its row is in `retarget-rows.json` (UB1.18). Section E's provider line now reads all five presets (owner 2026-10-02; UB6.2 amended) and its DEC-12 line the v0.15.1 relevance filter (UB6.16 amended).

W3 2026-10-16 (lane L-HOST2, Claude controller): (L-HOST2, 2026-10-16) REMAINDER LANDED in `bb8fcd362`, on top of `95f8f8b11`. This ports upstream v0.15.1's post-queue shape. When the layer is on, a text message that our own rules leave open is RECORDED AS QUEUED at once. Those rules exclude a runtime-own turn, a workflow invocation, a send that races send-start, a send after Stop, a send with an unsteerable row ahead, the user's one-message override and a host task notification. The ack never waits on the model. `steerQueuedIfDecided` then awaits the decision and the entry's continuation check. The decision now carries the running request: the latest delivered, visible user message that is not a task notification. It steers only while the entry is still queued, the same session and generation run, no Stop has happened since, no unsteerable row is ahead, the entry is not half of a continuation, and `agent.canSteerNow()` is true. The steer is recorded with `recordSteer` and the strip is told through `queue_changed`. `markQueuedContinuation` sets `mergeWith` by reference. `canMergeQueuedEntry` excludes a workflow invocation, a model text that differs from the display text, attachments, and hidden or task-notification rows. `processNextQueuedMessage` replays a continuation as one turn with the texts joined by a blank line, and every bubble moves to processing. The auth retry removes every merged bubble (`lastSentMergedMessageIds`/`replayMergedIds`). `canSteerNow` is an optional member on `AgentBackend`. Claude reads its open, unsettled slot and its unpaused inlined steer FIFO; there is no `pending-steers.ts` here. Pi uses upstream's read. Codex reports whether `turn/steer` can be sent, and codex then accepts or refuses natively (a refusal arrives as `steer_undelivered`). Two first-half defects are closed. A decided `queue` over a `steer` default used to stamp `wasInterrupted`; the stamp now reads the behaviour actually APPLIED. A decision could override a queue the host had forced, including the Claude case where a redirect without a slot kills the session; that is now gated by record-as-queued plus `canSteerNow`. Before UB2.10 the detached call's result was ALWAYS refused (falsely); now a revoke during no turn does not refuse it. Fix: retain the lease per detached requestId/taskId and release it on settle; then the detached path can keep assertActive. A detached MCP call settles with task_notification and never with task_completed, the only event that released a task authority. So the lease, and the plugin instance leases under it, stayed held until the agent was disposed. What landed: - SessionManager processEvent case task_notification: a kind-'mcp' task releases its authority. A workflow or subagent still lets go at its own task_completed. - PiAgent.handleToolExecuteRequest runs materializer.assertActive for a still-detached call again. Only the turn-identity check (manifest, runtime) stays skipped, as UB2.10 set it. - Both hot files keep their line count. Tests: - pi-detached-mcp-lease.test.ts (server-core, new): POSITIVE: the lease is retained past the turn end, a revoke then reads it inactive, and the task_notification releases it. BOUNDARY: a workflow task's task_notification releases nothing. 2 pass / 0 fail, 1 file. - pi-detached-tool-survives-stop.test.ts: the rig models the host lease. The new POSITIVE arm (a revoke after the turn ends refuses the late result as capability-snapshot-revoked) was red against HEAD's pi-agent.ts at 7/1. UB2.10's positive arm, now with the retain, is the NEGATIVE arm. - Shared neighbours: 94 pass / 0 fail, 5 files. Server-core neighbours: 35 pass / 0 fail, 4 files. - typecheck:shared and typecheck:server-core exit 0; eslint rc 0 from both package directories; diff --check clean. Residues: - A detach whose task_backgrounded the host never processed has no retained lease, so its result after the turn's end is refused. This is a tiny window: one synchronous write block. - A revoke while no turn runs refuses the late result but does not abort the running call (born, deferred). - Found and born CRITICAL, not fixed here: the 'mcp' piBackgroundTaskKinds entry is never deleted either, so the session never settles. No new sitting case is required. RS-127 arm C covers the unrevoked path in the packaged build. SITTING ASK: None required by the row. Start a slow MCP call past the R10 detach threshold, press Stop, and wait for the turn to end. 2. While no turn runs, revoke the call's capability (disable its source or uninstall its plugin) before the call settles. EXPECT: the task notification reports a failure carrying capability-snapshot-revoked, not the call's result. CONTROL: the same steps without the revoke report the result. That is RS-127 arm C. |

Its diagnosis did not hold. The L121 hook already has UB12.26's child-bun shape. What hid it is L99, `toMatch(/<svg[^>]*class="[^"]*…aria-hidden="true"/)`, which has five `"`. The scanner did not model regex literals, so the odd quote opened a "string" that ran to L150; the HEAD probe saw `beforeAll` code offsets only at L16 and L76, and no members. The fix teaches the scanner the form: a new `regexLiteralEnd` in scripts/check-module-graph-hooks.ts, a tokenizer look-behind. It is bounded to one line, so a misjudged `/` costs at most its line. codeTokenOffsets, splitCallArguments and withoutComments all call it. I chose this over editing the test file because the same blindness would drop a hook silently in a file that does not import the budget.
